reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - lovastatin significantly reduced cholesterol (-27.25 mg/dL) and LDL (-25.28 mg/dL), confirming HMG-CoA reductase inhibition. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed evidence of downstream pathway effects. Some biomarkers moved in expected directions (e-cadherin decreased in placebo vs increased in treatment, n-cadherin decreased in placebo vs increased in treatment), but others showed minimal changes (Ki-67, p21, HIF1alpha). The mevalonate pathway appears partially modulated but not consistently across all expected markers. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint failed - histopathologic regression of atypical nevi did not occur. Effect sizes were modest and inconsistent between pathologists (0.5 vs 0.17 for lovastatin, -0.12 vs 0.04 for placebo). No statistical significance reported. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Some suggestion of benefit in preventing nevi progression (1 vs 7 patients had increased nevi count with lovastatin vs placebo), but this was not the primary endpoint. 5. CONFOUNDERS: 24-week duration may have been insufficient for histopathologic changes in precancerous lesions. The endpoint relied on subjective pathologist assessment with inter-rater variability evident.

failure_modes.evidence: Target was clearly engaged (cholesterol/LDL reduction) and some downstream biomarkers moved (e-cadherin, n-cadherin), but the primary histopathologic regression endpoint failed to improve meaningfully
24 weeks may be insufficient for histopathologic regression of precancerous lesions, which could require longer treatment duration for structural tissue changes
